actions.action: Preserve focus by product and control identity
actions.mechanism: Stable DOM identity retains focus through reordering; a persistent results heading provides a predictable removal fallback.
actions.implementation: Key cards by product ID, never index. Preserve their controls. If the focused product disappears, focus the results heading with tabindex="-1".
actions.check: Reorder a focused product: its same control stays focused. Filter it out: focus reaches the heading. Filter-control focus never moves.
actions.risk: DOM moves can still disturb focus; test actual rendering behavior.

actions.action: Reject outdated updates without reclaiming focus
actions.mechanism: Request sequencing prevents stale results; commit-time focus inspection respects navigation performed while results were loading.
actions.implementation: Assign increasing request IDs. Commit only the latest response, updating cards and count together. Apply focus recovery only if focus remains inside affected results.
actions.check: Resolve two requests backward: only the latest appears. Move focus to a filter during loading: it stays there after completion.
actions.risk: Cancellation alone does not guarantee protection against stale responses.

actions.action: Keep the latest count immediately available
actions.mechanism: A persistent textual summary supports quick visual scanning and polite screen-reader notification without moving focus.
actions.implementation: Place a sticky count above results in a pre-existing role="status" region outside the busy results container. Update it with accepted results.
actions.check: Measure arrival-to-count rendering below one second. Verify accessible text updates within that interval and announcements do not steal focus.
actions.risk: Speech queues may delay announcements; sticky content must not obscure focus.

actions.action: Separate loading, empty, and failed states
actions.mechanism: Explicit state messages prevent an unfinished or failed request from being mistaken for zero matches.
actions.implementation: During requests, show “Updating results” and set results aria-busy="true". Label any retained count as previous. Show zero only after successful completion; provide keyboard-operable retry on failure.
actions.check: Delay, empty, and fail requests separately. Confirm distinct visible and accessible messages, and clear aria-busy on completion or failure.
actions.risk: Clearing existing cards while loading unnecessarily destroys user context.

actions.action: Expose the complete catalog in reading order
actions.mechanism: Native list semantics and consistent DOM order preserve browsing access independently of the visual grid.
actions.implementation: Render all 200 matching cards as list items, using CSS grid for layout. Keep DOM and visual order aligned; lazy-load images rather than product text or controls.
actions.check: Verify every matching product is reachable through screen-reader browsing and keyboard links, including the last item, before and after reordering.
actions.risk: Rendering every card requires profiling with realistic card complexity.

actions.action: Preserve viewport context around the focused product
actions.mechanism: Scroll compensation keeps a retained focused control near its previous screen position despite cards moving around it.
actions.implementation: Record the focused control’s viewport offset before committing results; afterward compensate scrolling without animation. For removed products, reveal the fallback heading instead.
actions.check: Reorder a retained focused product: it remains visible without focus changing. Remove it: the heading is visible. Verify behavior at 400% zoom.
actions.risk: Coordinate with browser scroll anchoring to avoid double compensation.
